bull_case: AI compute density drives a decade-long redesign of power and thermal architecture, and Vertiv becomes a preferred integrated supplier across hyperscale, colocation and enterprise critical infrastructure.
bear_case: The 2025-26 surge proves to be a concentrated AI capex cycle; hyperscalers standardize more of the stack and supplier competition compresses pricing as capacity catches up.
thesis: Vertiv has strong structural leadership in a secular architecture shift, not merely a normal equipment upcycle. Its breadth across AC/DC power, thermal management, liquid cooling, racks and service is difficult to replicate quickly. The score stops below the mid-80s because disclosed end-market concentration is not granular enough to prove multiple independent >10% demand pools, and hyperscalers retain substantial design and procurement power.

evidence.claim: Vertiv serves critical digital infrastructure across power management, thermal management, integrated rack solutions and services.
Backlog reached $15.0B at Dec. 31, 2025 versus $7.2B a year earlier, with most considered firm and expected within 12-18 months.
2026 organic sales growth guidance was 30%-32%, while Q2 sales grew 24.1% and operating profit 44.2% YoY.
Americas, Asia Pacific and EMEA provide geographic breadth, with 2025 sales mix approximately 62%, 20% and 18%.

counterevidence: A meaningful portion of incremental demand is tied to the same AI/hyperscale capex cycle, so geography is not independent demand diversification.
Large cloud and hyperscale customers have strong bargaining power and can delay or redesign projects.
Schneider Electric, Eaton and other global industrial competitors have comparable capital resources.
Backlog can create execution and fixed-price risk if input costs or customer schedules move.
unknowns: Revenue concentration by end market and top hyperscale customers.
Long-run share of AI data-center capex captured by Vertiv.
Normalized demand once current backlog growth slows.
Whether microgrid/behind-the-meter power becomes a genuinely independent demand pool.
falsifiers: If orders/backlog contract for several quarters while AI capex remains strong, category leadership should be cut.
If liquid-cooling and integrated-power content per rack keeps expanding across multiple customer types, secular durability rises.
If one customer/end market proves to represent >50% of economic growth, durability-risk score should fall.

subscores.rationale: AI rack density and power constraints require multi-year redesign of power and thermal infrastructure, with strong backlog and customer spending evidence.
Vertiv has global scale, broad product/service coverage and strong execution, but does not alone define hyperscaler architecture or industry standards.
Geographic and product breadth are real, but primary disclosures do not establish two or more independent final markets above the rubric's 10% threshold; AI/data-center demand remains correlated.

uncertainties.rationale: The current AI buildout is historically unusual and cycle length is uncertain.
Large customers influence specifications and multi-source supply.
End-market concentration is insufficiently disclosed for a higher rubric row.
